fullDescription: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Waves, a sine stack displaced by a warped phase. Six crests, each at its own frequency and speed, with the phase displaced by an anisotropic warp and a vertical light gradient behind them. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.
prompt:
## Resumo
A full-viewport animated WebGL fragment shader called Waves: a sine stack displaced by a warped phase. Six crests, each at its own frequency and speed, with the phase displaced by an anisotropic warp and a vertical light gradient behind them. The page contains nothing but the canvas. A shared GLSL preamble provides a hashed value noise, a six-octave fbm and a two-level domain-warp helper; this effect draws on them and adds its own body. Pointer movement raises a smoothed intensity uniform so the effect strengthens under the cursor and relaxes when it leaves.

## Estilo Visual
Ground #031017 with accents ["#C7F5FF", "#1A85B8"]. There is no typography and no page chrome: the shader is the entire surface. Keep the palette to two or three values so the effect reads as one material rather than a rainbow.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Canvas
One canvas fixed at inset 0 filling the viewport, with html and body at 100 percent height, margin 0 and overflow hidden. Behind it a hidden panel that is only shown when no WebGL context can be created.

### The shader
A sine stack displaced by a warped phase. Six crests, each at its own frequency and speed, with the phase displaced by an anisotropic warp and a vertical light gradient behind them.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Componente
Full-bleed fragment shader with no surrounding page

### Componente
Smoothed pointer-intensity uniform

### Componente
No-WebGL fallback panel

### Componente
Reduced-motion single-frame path
